name: THE ATRIUM
notes: Full replacement review proposal preserving project ID; building schema enables eight separately editable floors, doors, glazing and fixtures.
The concept contains 211 non-overlapping space rectangles across eight floors. Furnishings and openings are separate editable collections.
North is assumed at the top. Public arrival is from the west; ground-level loading enters from the east. Site roads, setbacks and external vehicle manoeuvring are outside this footprint.

Two stairs, two passenger lifts and one service lift align on all eight floors. West circulation serves guests; east circulation and the southern service corridor serve staff. Controlled crossover doors connect the routes.
Passenger lift doorways open west into the guest stair/core zone, which connects through the lobby and west circulation. Detailed lift lobbies and stair enclosures require professional development.

South-facing hotel accommodation is buffered by the service band; its daylight concept relies on borrowed light from glazed side circulation. Direct exterior glazing to every bedroom would require revising the perimeter circulation strategy.
Proposed hotel mix: seven keys on level 3, six on level 4, five on level 5 and two premium suites on level 6. A higher room count has not been assumed.
Ballroom A and B have an editable large connecting opening representing a retractable acoustic divider; partition storage, event capacity and AV layouts remain conceptual.
Level 2 has a genuine open terrace; level 7 has a separately reserved landscaped terrace. Waterproofing, drainage, guards and wind protection remain unresolved.
THE ATRIUM is treated as the hotel name; no multi-floor void is assumed because no atrium size or location was provided.
Room rectangles describe planning extents with 0.18 m internal walls. The intended 0.28 m external envelope requires a separate detailed envelope model.
All floor heights are assumed at 4 m. Convention clear heights, rooftop plant loads, structural transfers, wet-service risers, acoustic separation and kitchen exhaust routes require coordination.
Fixtures illustrate a low-density furnished concept, not a final seating, occupancy or equipment schedule. Toilet suites and staff WC/service rooms require further stall and privacy subdivision.
